title: 맞죠? 그렇죠?: -지요(-죠)로 확인하고 맞장구치기
objective: By the end, you can attach -지요/-죠 to verbs, adjectives, nouns, and past forms. You can use it to ask "..., right?" and to agree with what someone says.
summary: Use the ending -지요 (-죠) to check something you think is true and to agree with someone.

task.title: Check and agree with -죠
task.line: Read each item. Then write, choose, fix, or order the words so the sentence uses -죠 correctly.

forms.when: Present tense. Add it to the stem whether it ends in a vowel or a consonant. In speech, -지요 usually becomes -죠. Without 요, -지 is casual speech (반말) for close friends or younger people. With 요, -지요/-죠 is polite speech (존댓말) for teachers, older people, and people you don't know well.
forms.means: With a rising tone it means "..., right?". You think it is true and want the listener to agree.
forms.exampleMeaning: It's really hot today, isn't it?

forms.means: "..., didn't it?" Use it to check something that already happened.
forms.exampleMeaning: The movie we saw yesterday was fun, wasn't it?

forms.when: If the noun ends in a consonant, use 이죠. If it ends in a vowel, use 죠 (e.g. 친구죠).
forms.means: "It's N, right?" Use it to check a place, person, or thing.

forms.when: When you answer and agree with someone. 그렇죠 is a very common reply.
forms.means: "Yes, that's right." It shows you agree or that something is a known fact.
forms.example: A: 한국 음식 맛있죠? B: 그렇죠. 저도 정말 좋아해요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: Korean food is tasty, isn't it? B: It sure is. I really like it too.

watchOut: 학생죠 (X) → 학생이죠 (O): When a noun ends in a consonant, add 이 before 죠.
어제 많이 바쁘죠 (X) → 어제 많이 바빴죠 (O): If you are asking about the past, use -았/었죠.
사장님, 피곤하시지 (X) → 사장님, 피곤하시죠 (O): -지 without 요 is casual speech. Use -죠 with older people and people you don't know well.
exercises: Fill in the blank with -죠 (맵다): 이 김치찌개 좀 ____?
Fill in the blank with -죠 (예쁘다): A: 지난주에 제주도에 다녀왔어요. B: 와, 바다가 정말 ____?
Choose 죠 or 이죠: ① 저기가 우체국(죠 / 이죠)? ② 이 사람이 민지 씨 언니(죠 / 이죠)? ③ 저 하얀 건물이 도서관(죠 / 이죠)?
You are talking to your teacher. Choose the right one: 선생님, 오늘 오후에 수업 (있지 / 있죠)?
Find and fix the mistake: 어제 시험이 힘들죠? 저는 시간이 부족했어요.
Put the words in order to make a question: 커피 / 이 / 비싸죠? / 좀
answers: ① 이죠 ② 죠 ③ 이죠
